references.text: Joseph's prophecy about the seven years of famine that would follow the abundance – this is the prophecy directly fulfilled in verse 54.
Describes how the famine Joseph predicted spread across the whole earth, and people from all nations came to Egypt to buy grain.
Tells how the famine was very severe, so that both Egypt and Canaan were exhausted by it.
Stephen refers to the famine throughout Egypt and Canaan in his speech, highlighting Joseph's role in God's plan of salvation.
Describes a famine in the land that led Abram to Egypt – a pattern of famine affecting the movements of the patriarchs.
The psalmist refers to how God called a famine upon the land and cut off all supply of bread – a poetic account of the famine in Joseph's time.
The fulfillment of Joseph's prophecy that the abundance would be forgotten and the famine would consume the land.
The connection between the prophecy's warning of famine and the concrete rescue plan that was implemented.
Consequences of the crisis: The famine (41:54) led to all the land of Egypt becoming Pharaoh's property.
Reason for Egypt's preparedness: The gathering of food before the famine struck.
The first part of the prophecy (abundance), which is necessary to understand the second part (famine and preparedness).
